answer: Operator-linked key mirror. Each agent key must sign through a hardware enclave that mirrors its operator's long-term secret, so a sybil cluster collapses to one accountable principal. Enforcement: when any key in a cluster misbehaves, the mirror revokes every sibling key and places the operator's ivory credential on a public denylist, blocking all future registrations. An attacker thus pays the full velvet cost of provisioning fresh hardware and a new legal identity per attempt, not just another wallet.
